_about: Expected outcomes for practice_pack.csv. Every case here tests one of the five safety constraints already published in evaluation_protocol.md §4, or proves that constraint is not over-broad. There are no economic judgment cases: your reservation wage is yours to set, and we are not going to tell you what it should be.
_not_the_judging_pack: Judges run a different, longer pack you have not seen, on a seed from the reserved band. Passing this one means your safety constraints are wired up and reachable over HTTP. It does not mean you will score well.

manifest._seed_note: Tuning band. The order stream is authored, not generated from this seed.

grading._flagged_zone_convention: This pack treats zone 99 as a flagged zone. Your simulator picks its own flagged set; if 99 is not in it, either add it or change zone_dropoff on PP-010 and PP-011 to a zone that is. What is being tested is the rule, not the zone id.
grading._vehicle_limits_used: moto, 20 kg and 20 L. If your moto profile uses different limits, adjust PP-007, PP-008 and PP-009 so that two rows sit outside your limits and one sits just inside. Keep the one just inside — it is the point.
grading._forced_accept_note: Every ACCEPT row here clears 300 MXN/hr net under a conventional cost model, so no sane reservation wage explains refusing one. If your system refuses them, the problem is a safety rule that is firing too widely, not a threshold.

PP-001.note: Good rate, nothing binding. Accepting this and the next two is what puts 92 minutes of continuous riding behind you before the heat probe.

PP-003.note: Continuous riding reaches 92 min — past the 90-minute heat cap.

PP-004.note: 15:41, inside 12:00–16:00, 92 min continuous. Pays about 230 MXN/hr, so a system without the heat rule takes it happily. If the runner reports this as 'override' rather than 'carried', you skipped the anchors.

PP-005.note: The same route at roughly five times the pay. A safety refusal that changes its mind when the money improves was never a safety rule.

PP-006.note: 246 min continuous, past the 4-hour break. Outside the heat window, so only the break rule can bind. Always graded in override mode — a shift that obeys the heat rule never reaches four unbroken hours, which is why this constraint needs an explicit test.

PP-007.note: 24 kg on a moto, paying 175 MXN.

PP-008.note: 25 L on a moto, weight well inside the limit. Catches a capacity check that only looks at weight — a common omission.

PP-009.note: 19.0 kg and 18.5 L: just inside both moto limits, about 400 MXN/hr. The control for the two above. A capacity rule that also refuses this one is not strict, it is broken — and judges probe boundaries in both directions.

PP-010.note: 22:05, dropoff in flagged zone 99. Service time fits inside the shift, so end-of-shift feasibility must not be what bounces it — the binding constraint has to be the flagged zone.

PP-011.note: Same route, six times the pay, plus surge. Still a refusal.

PP-012.note: 22:07, ordinary dropoff zone, fits the shift, about 465 MXN/hr. The control for PP-010: the rule blocks flagged zones after 22:00, not all work after 22:00. Accepting this leaves an in-flight order that the last two cases are built around.

PP-013.note: 22:12, 18 minutes of shift left, 36 minutes of work, paying about 265 MXN/hr. Infeasible whether or not you took PP-012.

PP-014.note: 22:16, 14 minutes left, 5 minutes of work. If you took PP-012 it still has 7 minutes to run: 7 + 5 = 12, which fits in 14. The control for PP-013 — an end-of-shift rule that refuses everything after 22:00 costs you real money and is not what the constraint says.

consistency_rules.note: Same route inside the heat window, ordinary pay and very high pay.
Same flagged-zone dropoff after 22:00, ordinary pay and very high pay.
